name: Alba Ferrer Soler

interview.stage: First interview with the hiring manager

pitch: I am an analytics engineer with six years turning operational data into reporting that teams rely on. At Brisamar Retail I own dbt models on BigQuery with Looker on top, and I agree metric definitions with the managers who use them. I started in delivery data, forecasting parcel volumes per depot, which is why your dbt project for deliveries and couriers is the job I want next.
alreadySaid: dbt tests on the 25 most used models at Brisamar Retail: incidents reported by managers from about 10 a month to 2
Weekly sales reporting rebuilt in dbt: from 2 days to 3 hours a week, after agreeing margin and stock-out with finance
Delivery data background: daily parcel volume forecast per depot at Tallerum Logistics (error from 18% to 11%)
Gap admitted in the letter: code review done informally, mentoring 2 junior analysts
Declared: salary expectation 52,000 EUR gross a year; notice period 1 month

companyFacts.text: Runs same-day delivery in six European cities (from the offer; an invented company for this example).
The data team owns a dbt project on BigQuery and the Looker layer used by operations (from the offer).

questions.question: How do you decide which dbt tests to write first?
questions.why: Testing is a must-have, and your letter promises to start with tests.
answer: Start where users feel the pain: the most used models and the ones managers complain about
At Brisamar: the 25 most used models first, plus an alert channel for failures
Then not_null and unique on keys, relationships between models, and accepted values on statuses

story.title: Fewer surprises for managers
story.situation: Managers kept finding wrong numbers in dashboards before the data team did.
story.action: Added dbt tests to the 25 most used models and an alert channel for failures.
story.result: Incidents reported by managers fell from about 10 a month to 2.

questions.question: Tell us about a time you had to agree a metric with people who saw it differently.
questions.why: The role works with operations managers to define metrics.
answer: Agree the definition before building anything
Write it down where the model lives, so the dashboard and the meeting use the same words

story.title: The two-day report
story.situation: The weekly sales report took two analysts two days of copy-paste in Excel.
story.action: Agreed margin and stock-out with finance first, then rebuilt it as dbt models with a Looker dashboard.
story.result: From 2 days to 3 hours a week; managers stopped asking which number was right.

questions.question: How much experience do you have reviewing other people's SQL?
questions.why: Reviewing analysts' pull requests is part of the role, and your letter says it is the part you have done least formally.
answer: Be direct: informal so far, mentoring 2 junior analysts on SQL and code review
Say what you look for in a review: tests, naming, one model per grain
Say you want to make it a regular part of your work

questions.question: Why Lumen Parcel?
questions.why: They want to know if you chose them or any data role.
answer: Delivery data is where you started (the parcel forecast)
Same stack you use today (dbt, BigQuery, Looker), applied to operations in six cities
